name: ChatGPT-User

ips.note: Its address list is the longest of the three OpenAI files we counted: openai.com/chatgpt-user.json held 234 prefixes on 21 October 2026, creation time 2026-10-20, the day before this page. A list that long is a reason to fetch it again when you check a log line, not to copy it once into a firewall.

ua: Mozilla/5.0 AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko); compatible; ChatGPT-User/1.0; +https://openai.com/bot
vendor_quote: ChatGPT-User is not used for crawling the web in an automatic fashion. Because these actions are initiated by a user, robots.txt rules may not apply.
what_en:
Unlike the other OpenAI robots, ChatGPT-User does not roam the web by itself. OpenAI describes it as the agent used for certain user actions in ChatGPT and custom GPTs, including pages a custom GPT reaches through GPT Actions. A person typed something, and a request to your server followed.

| Fact | ChatGPT-User |
| --- | --- |
| Operator | OpenAI |
| Job | User-triggered fetch |
| robots.txt token | `ChatGPT-User` |
| Follows robots.txt | Robots.txt rules may not apply |
| Published address list | 234 ranges (openai.com/chatgpt-user.json, file dated 2026-10-20) |
| Vendor page read | 21 October 2026 |
block_en: Because the visit is user-initiated, OpenAI warns that robots.txt rules may not apply, so a `Disallow` line for ChatGPT-User is not a guaranteed stop. OpenAI also says ChatGPT-User is not used to decide whether content appears in search and sends search opt-outs to OAI-SearchBot. If you need to stop these requests, the control is on your server or CDN, not in robots.txt alone.
compare_en: OAI-SearchBot is the search crawler and does obey robots.txt.
answer_en: ChatGPT-User visits a web page when a person asks ChatGPT or a custom GPT a question that needs it. OpenAI says it is not used to crawl automatically and that, because a user starts the request, robots.txt rules may not apply. OpenAI lists 234 IP ranges for it.
title_en: ChatGPT-User: the fetcher that opens your page when someone asks
